production.note: US model years 2005-2010 for the 4.6-liter 3-valve GT. Start: Ford's 2005 brochure, 'The All-New 05MUSTANG'. Ford's 2009 brochure still lists the 300 hp GT (ford-mustang-brochure-2009) and the 2010 brochure rates the 4.6L at "315 hp @ 6000 rpm" (ford-mustang-brochure-2010). The 300 to 315 hp change (5%) on the same engine is not large enough for a separate record (data guide, year splits), so 2010 is included. The 2011-2014 5.0-liter GT, a different engine, is its own record.

body.note: Ford's 2009 brochure lists 'GT Coupe' and 'GT Convertible'; the 2006 brochure: 'Coupe or convertible, GT or V6' (ford-mustang-brochure-2006).

displacementL.note: Cars.com 2005 '2dr Cpe GT Deluxe': 'Displacement 4.6L/281' (281 cu in). Rob Rothwell, Auto123: '4.6L (281 cu in), 24-valve, SOHC V8' (auto123-mustang-gt-2005). No cc figure was found on an opened page.

transmission.note: Ford 2009 brochure, GT: standard "5-speed manual GT transmission (3.31:1 axle ratio)", option "5-speed automatic transmission". The 2005 brochure lists '5-speed manual GT transmission (3.55 axle ratio)' and '5-speed automatic transmission (3.31 axle ratio)'; Cars.com 2005 GT Deluxe: '5-Speed M/T', '5-Speed A/T' (cars-com-mustang-gt-2005).

powerHp.note: Quote (Ford 2005 brochure engine table, V6 column then V8 column): "Horsepower (hp @ rpm) 210 @ 5300 300 @ 5750". The 2006 brochure prints the same line (ford-mustang-brochure-2006) and the 2009 brochure gives the GT's "4.6L SOHC 3-valve V8300 hp @ 5750 rpm" (ford-mustang-brochure-2009), so the rating was 300 hp for 2005-2009. 2010: 315 hp @ 6000 rpm (ford-mustang-brochure-2010); 300 hp covers five of the six years, so the reference year is the launch year.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (database and single articles). 2005 GT coupe. Quote (Cars.com 2005 '2dr Cpe GT Deluxe', the transmission is not stated): "Base Curb Weight 3,450 lbs". Rob Rothwell, Auto123 2005 Mustang GT road test (2-door coupe, 5-speed manual): "Curb Weight: 1,563 kg (3,445 lbs)" (auto123-mustang-gt-2005). John Heilig, The Auto Channel, 2005 Mustang GT (5-speed manual), body text: 'the 3,450-lb. Car' (not labelled curb; theautochannel-mustang-gt-2005). CJ Pony Parts gives 3,483 lb for every 2005-2009 GT coupe (see discrepancies). Ford's 2005, 2006 and 2009 brochures print no weight.

discrepancies.reason: Cars.com (3,450 lb) and Auto123's spec panel (3,445 lb, from 1,563 kg) agree within 0.2%; CJ Pony Parts lists 3,483 lb for every 2005-2009 GT coupe without naming the transmission. The spread is 1.1%.
discrepancies.resolution: 3,450 lb used: Cars.com's figure for the 2005 GT Deluxe coupe, matched by Auto123 and by Heilig's text; all are provisional figures.

provisionalNote: Weight (3,450 lb) rests on Cars.com (database) and single articles (Auto123 spec panel 3,445 lb; John Heilig's text 3,450 lb), with CJ Pony Parts at 3,483 lb. Ford's 2005-2009 brochures print no weight. A Ford curb weight (press kit or technical specifications) or a major magazine spec panel would replace it. Power is from Ford brochures.
